extracted.intended_audience: performers/producing companies seeking programming at Pleasance and audience ticket-buyers (Edinburgh Fringe and Pleasance London)
extracted.subtask_short: Pleasance Fringe programming and venue policies
extracted.subtask_description: Official Pleasance FAQ covering ticketing, admission, programming submissions, technical requirements and artist support for shows at Pleasance venues (Edinburgh Fringe and London). Useful for performers applying to the festival and audience members buying tickets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Booking methods and box office hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Tickets can be booked online 24/7 through the website or by calling box office phone lines; in-person sales available around show times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box office phone hours vary around show times; typical availability: weekdays from 2pm until late, Saturdays from 12pm until late, phone lines closed on Sundays unless a show is on. The box office closes 15 minutes after the final performance of the day. Advance booking is encouraged to avoid disappointment; the online transaction itself is instant so booking close to start time may be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-ticketing (definition, default delivery, and practical use)
rubrics_metrics.description: An e-ticket is an electronic ticket: a QR code in your confirmation email serves as your ticket for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-ticketing is the default option (introduced 2022) and printing has been reduced for sustainability. Any device with access to your email inbox is acceptable for scanning; it's better to show the entire confirmation email rather than a fixed screenshot of the QR code. If confirmation isn't received, check spam/junk and resend from 'my orders' in your account or contact [email protected]. You may forward your e-ticket to a friend; note a transaction barcode can grant entry to all shows contained in the email confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: If QR code / confirmation issues arise
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for when the QR code won't load or confirmation email is missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access QR code by logging into your Pleasance account and re-sending the confirmation email from 'your orders'. Check spam/junk first; add [email protected] to contacts. If issues persist, email [email protected] for troubleshooting assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission ID checks and concession verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Venue staff may sight ID to verify concession tickets or when purchasing alcohol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carrying ID is recommended as entry or concession admission may be refused without proof; a refund will not be given in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latecomer policy and arrival recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Latecomer admission is subject to artists' policies and venue terms; latecomers may be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latecomer policies are set by performing artists to avoid disruption; many shows have strict no-latecomer policies with no refunds. Arrive approximately 30 minutes before the publicised start time. If latecomers are allowed, you may be asked to wait outside until the appropriate late-entry point. For specific show rules contact the box office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds (non-refundable tickets)
rubrics_metrics.description: All tickets (including booking fees) are strictly non-refundable as per terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do not offer refunds on tickets, merchandise or vouchers. Handling/booking fees are non-refundable in the event of a performance cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticket exchanges (discretionary and conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance may offer discretionary exchanges if specific conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: request made at least 48 hours before the original performance start time; emailed to [email protected]; original performance not sold out; exchange is for the same show on a different time/day; exchange tickets must be equal or higher value (customer pays difference if higher; no refund if lower). Exchanges incur a fee of £1.25 per ticket (capped at £5), payable over the phone and settled at least 24 hours before the original performance; exchanges cannot be processed via email or in person. Exchanges are subject to availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling/booking fees and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling fees apply to bookings to cover payment gateways and related costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online/phone handling fee: £1.50 per ticket, capped at £6 across a transaction (4 tickets). In-person counter sales: reduced fee £1 per ticket, capped at £5. Fees are charged to contribute toward charges associated with online bookings and ticketing infrastructure; Pleasance does not include booking fees in listed ticket price to avoid penalising performing companies. Fees are non-refundable on show cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash acceptance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether venues accept cash varies by site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edinburgh: one till at main Pleasance Courtyard and Pleasance Dome box offices accepts cash; other concessions are card only. London: Pleasance London is fully cashless and does not accept cash on site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Babes in arms and child ticketing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Babes in arms are defined as infants under 2 years who sit on a parent's lap; ticket requirements vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where babes in arms are permitted, under-2s do not require a ticket; all children aged 2+ require a ticket. Policies vary by show and venue; check with box office. Babes in arms are not permitted at the Edinburgh International Conference Centre (EICC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Baggage, cloakroom and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited space; no on-site cloakroom or luggage storage during performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasance cannot store luggage; recommend travelling light and keeping valuables with you. Buggy parking is limited (see Kidzone and Grand Box Office in Courtyard) and offered first-come-first-served—Pleasance is not responsible for possessions left there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age guidance vs age restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Age suitability labels are split into guidelines and restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guideline means under-age people may watch; a restriction means no one under the specified age will be admitted. For restricted shows FOH will check ID of anyone who looks under the rating; bring ID as you may be refused entry without it and no refund will be available. Always check both age guidance and content warnings before booking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resale prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Resale of tickets via third parties or secondary markets is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any booker found re-selling tickets will have the original booking cancelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online account management (email updates and troubleshooting)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to update account email address and re-send confirmations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To update an email address call the box office or email [email protected]. After changes, log out and log back in so updates pull through. Use 'my orders' to re-send confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Under-18 site access and supervision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 18s must be accompanied by an adult on Pleasance sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 18 year olds must be accompanied by an adult at all times on Pleasance sites and when watching shows. Accompanied children are prohibited from being directly in front of or near bar areas. 0–16 year olds are allowed on premises only until midnight and must be accompanied by an adult; 16 and 17 year olds may be on site during all operation hours if accompanied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-venue drinks policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about taking purchased drinks between Pleasance venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you buy a drink at the main Courtyard bar you can take it to The Grand, Baby Grand or Bunker only if heading directly to your venue. In other cases drinks cannot be consumed outside Pleasance premises or taken off site. For Potterrow Plaza to Dome: you can cross directly into the Dome if heading directly to see a show; otherwise, drinks cannot be consumed outside or taken off site.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to begin a Fringe submission (Performer Information Pack)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start the application process by reading the Performer Information Pack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Performer Information Pack contains a full rundown of what it means to bring a show to the festival with Pleasance and detailed practical information (technical specs, deposits, deals, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and getting a slot (rolling submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance programmes on a rolling submission basis and requires a submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the submission form (found on Perform With Us) to be considered. The form helps track the process and provides necessary information for decision-making. You can submit whether you're a veteran, touring company or newcomer; prior Pleasance performance is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting multiple shows
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply with more than one show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each show requires a separate submission; Pleasance accepts multiple submissions from the same applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of work Pleasance programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance presents a wide range of genres but rarely programmes revivals or amateur productions of established texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They programme comedy, text-based and physical theatre, family and children's work, circus, dance and cabaret. Careful consideration is needed for technical/space requirements especially for circus/dance/cabaret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for new work and policy on previously performed shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is given to work premiering at the Fringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They sometimes programme returning shows that were successful with Pleasance previously or had successful runs in other venues, but priority to new work means returning shows are usually confirmed late in the process (around late March/early April).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short runs and how run length affects programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Short runs are more difficult to finalise than full runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority of shows perform for the full festival to make the most impact; shorter runs are possible but tend to be confirmed later as time needs to be found for technical rehearsals and slot-filling mid-festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission receipt confirmation and adding info
rubrics_metrics.description: You should receive a confirmation email with a copy of your submission; you can add information later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't get a confirmation, check spam/junk; if absent, Pleasance likely did not receive submission. To add info, respond to the confirmation email with updates or supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curated programming (not first-come, first-served)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance curates a balanced programme across styles, topics and voices rather than operating on a first-come-first-served basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They aim for a diverse programme so some shows take longer to confirm; programming is rolling through to the brochure deadline (early/mid April). If you have another offer you can contact programmers and they may be able to respond sooner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to apply to multiple Fringe venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying to multiple venues is allowed and encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasance expects applicants to apply elsewhere because slots are limited. They may be able to accelerate decisions if you have other offers—contact programmers at the provided emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access and disability enquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance encourages discussion of specific access requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact [email protected] or phone 020 7619 6868. An Artist Access Guide provides more details on accessibility for their spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback on submissions (limited capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance does not provide feedback on individual submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to the high volume of submissions they cannot offer individual feedback on applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial deal with visiting companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Pleasance financial deal is a split of box office revenue in favour of the visiting company, with a minimum guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard split: 60/40 in visiting company's favour, set against a minimum guarantee based on Pleasance's share at 40% capacity. For non-VAT registered companies the split is 55/45. Full guide in the Performer Information Pack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-front costs, marketing contra and deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: There are up-front costs to accept a slot including Fringe registration fee, marketing contra and deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard marketing contra is £630. Deposits are charged at point of accepting a slot and are based on venue size and run length—details and deposit estimates are in the Performers' Information Pack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasance-managed Fringe Society registration
rubrics_metrics.description: If programmed, Pleasance will manage your registration with the Fringe Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They will provide an overview of the process when you are programmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasance support services for companies during Fringe
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance provides infrastructure and services to support companies before and during the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support includes Arts Industry Reception (industry/guest ticketing coordination), Press Office (press enquiries, press tickets, marketing surgeries), Playwell x Pleasance Preventative Care Programme, Pleasance Producers and other artist development resources. Companies are expected to match this with their own investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical: selecting an appropriate space
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a space balancing technical ambition with realistic sales expectations—the playing area generally scales with capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Edinburgh Fringe Spaces page for venue sizes and layouts; ensure technical ambition matches likely ticket sales and capacity of chosen space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical rehearsals: scheduling and allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: For full festival runs, technical rehearsals typically take place the Sunday, Monday and Tuesday before the first preview on Wednesday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact slots are confirmed when the programme is finalised and technical information is received; confirmations usually start late-May. Arrive earlier if technically ambitious to secure more tech time. Shows starting mid-festival will tech within performance schedules; programming team allocates slots for late starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection and video usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Projection is possible in some venues; video equipment is not standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where projection is not possible a plasma screen may be used. If projection is essential include this in technical information and discuss with programmer—shows requiring projection may be prioritised for end-on spaces. Video kit is not standard and is provided/charged based on estimated demand; check tech specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue plans and technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Venue plans and tech specs are available on the Edinburgh Fringe Spaces page; Vectorworks (.vwx) files available on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files may change slightly during build; for Vectorworks files email the Edinburgh technical team. Always consult current tech specs for rigging, capacities and standard kit lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring technical equipment through suppliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment can be hired through Pleasance's lighting, sound and video suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate cards are provided; rates are renegotiated annually and subject to change. If multiple companies use the same kit costs may be split; technical team will try to find cost-effective solutions. Video kit costs are already split across venues to provide upfront quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bringing personal technical equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing your own equipment is allowed but generally discouraged in favour of hiring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring allows pre-rigging and efficiencies. Personal kit must be fit for purpose, PA tested and signed off by Pleasance technical team before use. Pleasance can guarantee functionality of hired equipment and respond quickly to issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operators (lights/sound) provision and charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance can provide operators for shows, with charges depending on the level of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Lights up/Lights down' operator is available at £20 + VAT per operator per performance. 'Full show' operation available in larger spaces at Pleasance's discretion and is charged at £30 + VAT per operator per performance. If no operator stays for a full month provide a detailed script, allow shadowing time, and 'lock' the show before leaving. Shows dependent on sound mixing or live music are advised to provide their own operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround times between shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Turnaround times vary by venue size and are shared between companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turnarounds range from around 15 minutes in smallest venues to 60 minutes in largest venues; these include audience exit/entry time and are shared responsibilities between both performing companies rather than split halves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing venue layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally not possible to change or reset a venue layout within the turnaround timeframe without sign-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change to layout or capacity must be signed off by programming and technical teams and must maintain safe evacuation routes at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of naked flames and smoke effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Naked flame is possible in some Courtyard venues subject to rigorous approval; not allowed in the Dome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires sign-off by the technical team, appropriate risk assessments and method statements, a visit from senior team and possibly a University Fire Marshall during tech slot. RAMS (Risk Assessment and Method Statements) must be current and adhered to, with checks in the run-up to the performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue crew allocation and expectations of company staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each venue has a dedicated technical team whose size varies; companies are expected to bring their own core personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are guaranteed a dedicated crew member plus someone covering shared venues; teams rotate so same individuals are not guaranteed for all performances. Venue teams support the smooth running but Pleasance expects each show to have its own stage manager/performer/producer or other team as the venue team cannot be relied upon solely to deliver the show's technical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: QLab provision and recommendations for shows using video
rubrics_metrics.description: Each venue runs a Mac Mini for QLab as standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows using video on QLab should bring an additional machine or hire one to support extra processing required for video and sound output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All companies are required to have public liability insurance with a minimum indemnity limit of £5 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasance accepts Equity membership as insurance for performers, but Equity cover only the performer—if multiple performers, each must have membership. Equity does not cover props/equipment; consider a separate show policy especially if props or audience participation are involved. Pleasance's insurance covers equipment hired through them but not loss, theft or damage of personal equipment; Pleasance cannot be held liable for personal equipment loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical differences at EICC
rubrics_metrics.description: EICC venues are built and run by EICC's in-house team and differ slightly in technical management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical correspondence for EICC sites will involve both the EICC team and Pleasance; contact the programming team for queries specific to EICC.

rubrics_metrics.name: London programming: seasons, spaces and hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance London curates seasonal programmes across comedy, theatre, drag and cabaret and also hires spaces for private events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three performance spaces: Main House, Downstairs and Studio. Pricing and financial deals depend on season and event specifics—contact Pleasance for hire availability and quotes. Programming and hires are typically confirmed 3–12 months in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasance role in producing work
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance primarily operates as a receiving house rather than producing in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They co-produce and support work through artist development opportunities in various formalised ways—see Artist Development page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script reading and unsolicited feedback policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance has limited capacity to read unsolicited scripts or provide feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They accept script excerpts as part of wider applications for opportunities but generally cannot provide specific feedback due to volume and staff limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasance staff attendance at external shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance programmers and team regularly attend work across London, nationally and sometimes internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a show you want Pleasance to see, contact the relevant email (comedy or theatre/cabaret/drag addresses provided) with details and how you'd like to get involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist development support and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance offers artist development support and communicates opportunities through channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit the Artist Development page for detailed opportunities. Follow their artist development X account and sign up to the Pleasance newsletter to keep up to date with upcoming opportunities.
